newsitem.title: INDIA: India says 96/97 revised GDP growth at 6.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: India says 96/97 revised GDP growth at 6.8 pct.

text.p: India's revised estimate for gross domestic product growth in 1996/97 (April-March) was 6.8 percent, unchanged from an earlier estimate, the government said in a statment on Wednesday.

"Although there is no change in the growth at overall level, major changes in the growth rate are visible at sectoral level, in agricutlture, forestry and fishing (now estimated at 5.7 percent as compared to 3.7 percent earlier) and in manufacturing (now estimated at 8.1 percent as compared to 10.6 percent estimated earlier)," the statement said.
The GDP for 1996/97 was now estimated at 2,928.18 billion rupees at 1980/81 prices, compared with the earlier estimate of 2,929.33 billion, the statement said.

The real GDP growth figures, representing changes from the previous 1995/96 fiscal year, were at constant (1980/81) prices, the government said in the statement on a quarterly update of growth figures by the Central Statistical Organisation (CSO).
The earlier estimates, called the advanced estimates, were released in January.
The statement said the revised 1996/97 growth estimates for some other sectors were as follows:

Mining and quarrying 1.0 percent; electricity, gas and water supply 3.8 percent; construction 5.5 percent; trade, hotels, transport and communication 8.7 percent; financing, insurance, real estate and business services 6.9 percent; community, social and personal services 5.3 percent.
The statement did not give the earlier estimates for these sectors. ($1=35.7 rupees)
